A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the regional employment prognosis, which was carried out in the framework of the REGARIS project, has proved its worth as a method of analysis, but not as a method of prognosis.
the regional employment forecasts for the old federal states are a valuable basis for regional labour market policy, especially for the decentralisation planned in the Employment Promotion Reform.
the shift-share analysis has a limited value for forecasting purposes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the effects of the minimum wage on the employment of the young, low skilled, and the old are small and not significant.
the effects of the 2008-2009 financial crisis and the Great Recession on the labor market were much less pronounced than in the previous recessions of the 1970s and 1990s.
